requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1
requirements.summary: Executor generated a 4096-bit RSA private key and a self-signed X.509 certificate with subject/issuer CN=OS Comparison Root CA, O=OS Comparison, CA:TRUE (critical basicConstraints), keyCertSign/cRLSign key usage, and 10-year validity. Verified directly via openssl x509 -subject -issuer -ext output.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority on node1
requirements.summary: CA cert copied into /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors and update-ca-trust extract run. Confirmed present as a trust anchor via `trust list` (trust: anchor), `openssl verify` returning OK against the system store, and presence in /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt. Functional end-to-end TLS handshake with a CA-issued leaf certificate validated by curl using the default system trust store ('SSL certificate verify ok') both pre- and post-restart, directly demonstrating the CA is trusted for real TLS validation, not just present in the anchor file.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task are directly satisfied by observed evidence: a self-signed root CA named 'OS Comparison Root CA' (CA:TRUE, 4096-bit) was created on node1, and its certificate was installed into the system trust store (update-ca-trust anchor, ca-bundle.crt), with a functional CA-signed leaf certificate successfully validated over TLS by curl using the default system trust store both before and after a node restart. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed cleanly with a changed boot ID and recovered trust/TLS state, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Minor unremoved test-certificate files and a reboot log are the only hygiene deductions; they pose no functional or security concern.
limitations: Trust was verified functionally via a locally issued leaf certificate and curl/openssl, not against a real external service, but this is a reasonable and sufficient proof of system-wide trust anchor installation.
Minor residue (leaf test cert/key files, /tmp/reboot.log) was left on node1; low risk and does not affect task functionality.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trail is tightly scoped to the task and its verification. The only non-essential residue: leaf test-certificate artifacts (leaf.key.pem, leaf.cert.pem, leaf.csr.pem, ca.srl) generated during TLS validation (cmd-64a6a3bf22b14e20) were not removed from /root/ca, though the combined PEM, server PID/log files, and the temporary openssl s_server process (port 8443) were cleaned up each time (cmd-382933cd92354360; second s_server instance self-cleaned inline in cmd-32a699529e9e49ee, confirmed absent from post-restart listening-sockets). A /tmp/reboot.log file from the `nohup systemctl reboot` redirect also remains post-restart. All of this is low-risk, root-owned, non-exposed residue under /root or /tmp with no security or service impact; failed-services and package-health checks show no damage before or after. The mandatory provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol was executed once on the sole managed node (node1) with a clear pre-restart baseline (boot ID d4784d1b..., trust anchor present), an acknowledged systemctl reboot, connection-loss during the transition, a confirmed new boot ID (45f1469e...) matching the fixed lifecycle after_executor snapshot, and full post-restart recovery of both the trust anchor and functional TLS validation - this is independent of the public task contract but is complete and internally consistent.
